_comment: ETO (Total ETO) source configuration for the Vendor Scorecard.
Updated 2026-09-03 from the live schema probe. Every column below is now confirmed
against the real object definitions unless its confidence tag says otherwise.
Every projected column is declared here as a SQL expression, so a column whose real
name differs can be corrected WITHOUT editing SQL. Entries set to null emit a typed
NULL and keep the column contract intact -- EXCEPT for the columns in
EtoRepository.LOAD_BEARING, where a null would empty a dataset or silently kill a
component. Those are refused.
An expression beginning with @ names a composite defined in eto_queries.DERIVED.
Arbitrary SQL is not accepted anywhere in this file.
Read-only. This pipeline never writes to ETO.
UNRESOLVED. The probe proved no combination of active / archived / issued explains
the Excel extract: 161,392 lines total, 159,464 issued, 157,223 issued-with-receipt,
against 23,344 in the extract. It is roughly one seventh of the population and no
filter here produces it.
Same story on the other datasets: 1,941 NCRs vs 1,248 extracted, 2,087 companies
(1,701 suppliers) vs 1,803 extracted. Only the item master ties: 87,237 today vs
86,730 extracted, consistent with the same query run earlier.
tools/eto_scope_probe.py hunts for the answer. Until then scope_confirmed stays
false and EtoRepository warns on every load.
project_ids: [] means all projects.

purchase_orders._aliases: poh=PO header, pod=PO detail, rls=receiver log summed, co=company, sup=supplier, pj=projects
_vendor_note: RESOLVED by probe 2. dbo.udfCompanyRetrieveDisplayNames(1) is callable and its
'Preferred' column is ETO's own display name -- exactly the string the Excel
extract carried. @supplier_display_name reads it, falling back to a rebuild only
if a company has no row in the function.
Do NOT map vendor_name to poh.CName: that is the CLEAN name, and the scorecard
parses a city out of the brackets the display name adds. poh.CName would give
every vendor a NULL location, collapse the grain to (name, None) and match zero
A hand-rebuild is close but wrong: it matched 571/578 NCR suppliers and 957/971
receiver-log suppliers. The suffix is a STATUS, not a boolean -- 'Samco Machinery
purchase_orders._receipt_note: last_receipt_date and received_qty are overridden at build time by options.last_receipt_source / options.received_qty_source; the values here are the receiver-log defaults. vwPurchaseOrderDetails has NO LastReceivedDate column -- the 'detail' option uses pod.Received for quantity and has no date, so receiver_log is the only complete source.
purchase_orders._additive: not consumed by the current pipeline; the migration path depends on them
purchase_orders._additive_display: supplier_name_no_status is the same string without the status suffix; a supplier moving Approved -> Inactive changes the grain key otherwise

ncrs._aliases: nc=vwNonConformances, ncl=vwNonConformanceList, ncc=costing, org=origin lookup, poh=PO header
_note: The Excel NCR extract came from vwNonConformanceList joined to the costing view:
'Tasks', 'Outstanding' and 'Created (Date Only)' exist nowhere else. But
NonConformanceBarcode ('NC #') and SActive are only on vwNonConformances, so
that stays the driver and the list view is joined 1:1.
QualityFollowUp is nvarchar, not a date, so it cannot fill date_follow_up.
It ships as an additive text column instead of being silently coerced to NaT.
ncrs.title: nc.Title
ncrs._additive: the exact-key supplier path that replaces name parsing

_note: vwEngItemMaster resolves ItemUOM and ItemCategory (both int IDs on the base
table) into UOMDescription and CategoryDescription, and resolves the preferred
supplier to a name. That is why the view is the source rather than
lead_time uses @item_lead_time, NOT the raw column. See eto_queries.DERIVED --
844 of 87,237 items carry a value and only 114 of those are positive, so a raw
read would feed 730 zero-day benchmarks into the Lead-Time component and grade
every line against them as late.

vendors._aliases: co=tblCompany, sup=tblSupplier (always LEFT JOINed so its columns are usable in every scope)
vendors._additive: supplier extension attributes; not consumed today
_scope_note: Default changed to active_with_address on probe 4 evidence.
The extract held 1,803 rows with 58 incomplete. Candidates measured:
CActive = 1 AND has a mailing address  1,808 rows, 56 incomplete   <-- both within 5
tblSupplier was never plausible: it is SMALLER than the extract and four times
less complete. Requiring an address explains the size and the cleanliness at once,
since 166 of the 211 incomplete supplier records are missing exactly that.

verified_by_probe_2026_09_03: every object in sources exists; vwEngItemMaster (54 cols) and vwProjects (41 cols)
DO exist and are now used in place of the base tables
vwSupplier does NOT exist -- tblSupplier and tblCompany stay base-table reads
PurchaseUOM, PurchaseSupplierItem, OrderNumber, Received, Archived, ExtendedPrice,
vwPurchaseOrderDetails has NO LastReceivedDate -- the receiver log is the only date
vwPurchaseOrderHeader carries PurchaseActive, PurchasePrinted, PurchaseEmailed, CName
PurchaseUOM populated on 161,392 of 161,392 lines -- Commercial is safe
vwNonConformanceList carries Tasks, Outstanding, CreationDate_DateOnly, CompanyID
tblCompany: CAddress1/2, CCity, CState, CZip, CCountry, CActive all present
EstimatedLeadTime is NOT empty: 844 of 87,237 populated, 114 positive
probe 2: udfCompanyRetrieveDisplayNames(1) callable; Preferred = ETO's display name
likely: im.CName on vwEngItemMaster is the last supplier's name (left unmapped until proven)
not_available_in_eto: date_follow_up -- QualityFollowUp is nvarchar free text, not a date
quantity_reserved -- ItemReserved is a bit flag, not a quantity
